proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity of an obligation to bind, constrain, or direct action. It is internally grounded in the obligation (and ultimately in the bearer of the obligation), it is not always manifested (one may have an obligation whose force is never acted upon), and it can be realized in processes of compliance or enforcement. This profile matches BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): a realizable entity that is internally grounded in the bearer's structure and that is realized in processes. It is distinct from Role (externally grounded) and Quality (a fully occurrent measurable property). The existing class LegalObligation already captures the obligation itself; NormativeForce would be a distinct SDC inhering in the bearer of the obligation, representing the binding capacity.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), as it is a realizable, internally grounded capacity inhering in a bearer.
RETRACTED — NormativeForce does not subclass LegalObligation; it inheres in the bearer of a LegalObligation. This relation should not be committed; see open_questions.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce be modeled as inhering in the agent who bears the LegalObligation (i.e., the obligated person), or in the LegalObligation instance itself? BFO requires dispositions to inhere in material entities; if LegalObligation is itself an SDC, we need to identify the ultimate material bearer for NormativeForce.
Is 'normative force' intended as a general philosophical concept (a class) or as the specific normative force of a particular obligation (an individual)?

Should NormativeForce be distinguished from LegalLegitimacyCondition (already in ontology as BFO_0000016)? The two are related but LegalLegitimacyCondition seems to be a condition on the system, while NormativeForce is a capacity of a specific norm.
The second relation proposed above (NormativeForce subClassOf LegalObligation) is incorrect and should NOT be committed — please disregard it. It was flagged for retraction within the same response.
proposal.rationale_summary: The question asks which BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation.' Normative force is the binding, action-guiding capacity that an obligation carries — it is not merely a static measurable property (ruling out Quality, BFO_0000019), nor is it externally conferred by social recognition alone (ruling out Role, BFO_0000023). It is best understood as an internally grounded, realizable capacity: the obligation has the disposition to bind its bearer, which is realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or resistance. This maps squarely onto BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016). A new class NormativeForce is proposed as a subclass of Disposition. The erroneous subClassOf relation to LegalObligation included in the relations array should not be committed; the correct ontological link is RO_0000052 (inheres in) between an instance of NormativeForce and the material bearer of the obligation, not a subsumption relation.
